# MLflow Trace Archival Benchmark

> This independent benchmark measures how long PostgreSQL takes to select traces for MLflow to archive. It checks the order of trace IDs and measures how concurrent span writes affect selection and ingestion.

The SQL study uses a reduced schema and measures server planning and execution time. The finder and ingestion studies run MLflow 3.18.0 against tables created by its migrations and measure complete selection transactions.

## Get started

- [Read a saved report](https://kenchengkc.github.io/mlflow-trace-archive-bench/#quick-start): Inspect the million-trace run with Git and Python 3.10 or later.
- [Run a local benchmark](https://kenchengkc.github.io/mlflow-trace-archive-bench/#local-benchmark): Compare three queries on two 1,000-trace PostgreSQL queues.
- [Contribute](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kenchengkc/mlflow-trace-archive-bench/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): Install PostgreSQL, run the tests, and report a result.

## Study guides

- [SQL query strategies](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kenchengkc/mlflow-trace-archive-bench/main/results/strategy-study/README.md): Compare the global query, the per-experiment query, and the bounded probe on different archive layouts.
- [MLflow’s candidate finder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kenchengkc/mlflow-trace-archive-bench/main/results/finder/README.md): Compare raw SQL and driver timings. Check query counts and trace order at 1,000 and 1,001 experiments.
- [Concurrent trace ingestion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kenchengkc/mlflow-trace-archive-bench/main/results/ingestion/README.md): Compare selection latency and ingestion throughput. Follow a span write through serialization, database execution, and commit.

## Optional

- [SQL timing table](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kenchengkc/mlflow-trace-archive-bench/main/results/strategy-study/matrix.md): Compare all 45 combinations of experiment scope, batch size, and archive depth.
- [Raw results](https://github.com/kenchengkc/mlflow-trace-archive-bench/tree/main/results): Read the compressed JSON measurements, query plans, and ordering checks.
